beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A result can be reproduced while its relationship to a prose claim remains implicit.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book proposes recording the semantic dependencies connecting evidence, assumptions, methods, and conclusions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A corrected dataset can then identify which dependent claims require renewed attention.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Affected does not automatically mean false, and the book preserves that distinction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A reviewer can challenge a particular dependency instead of rejecting an entire narrative.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The chapter develops this semantic build system as a companion to scientific explanation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Making a dependency explicit does not decide whether an institution should accept it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A formal representation can preserve an unfair category or a mistaken source.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book treats governance and contested definitions as part of the design problem.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It also makes room for unknown results and unresolved disagreement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A reader evaluating automated review can use these distinctions to question impressive demonstrations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ask what the representation preserves and who approved its commitments.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The scientific application becomes more useful when its legitimate limits remain visible.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The research programme measures false assurance as well as task accuracy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An answer can be wrong because it claims stronger support than the process warrants.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Comparisons include structured output, established knowledge standards, and direct translation into formal targets.
